answer: Verifiable delay functions curb Sybil attacks by linking agent validity to sequential proofs seeded by a randomness beacon. Upon each synchronization pulse, an agent must traverse a computational terrace of non-parallelizable puzzles to retain active status. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicating distinct single-threaded CPU cores per identity. A key limitation is that custom low-latency hardware allows well-funded adversaries to evaluate steps faster than commodity chips.
